round4.prereg_text:
# Round 4 pre-registration: bigger scan universe (written before any round-4 result was computed)
Written: Oct 26, 2026 ~10:20 PM PT. Protocol identical to rounds 1-2 unless stated (research2.py engine reused unchanged).

## Question
Does the live Pullback rule, and its momentum Grade A, still hold out of sample on a larger universe of liquid
large caps and ETFs? If yes (and data/runtime are reliable), the live scanner may use the larger universe.

## Universe U4 (fixed now, not edited after results)
* S&P 100 constituents as listed on Wikipedia on Oct 26 2026 (101 symbols). GOOG dropped (duplicate share class of GOOGL);
  BRK.B written BRK-B for Yahoo.
* 15 ETFs: SPY QQQ IWM DIA XLK XLF XLE XLV XLI XLP XLY XLU XLB XLRE XLC.
* Plus every one of the current 23 (adds SPCX, CCI, SBAC, which are not in the S&P 100).
* Tickers with no Yahoo data are dropped and listed. Tickers join the momentum ranking once they have 252 bars (as before).

## Data / protocol (unchanged)
Yahoo daily bars, split+dividend adjusted, max history, cached to research/data4/. TRAIN 2005-01-01..2022-12-31,
TEST 2023-01-01..data end. Signals at close t use bars <= t; entry at the close (robustness: next open).
Exit first close > SMA(5) or 10 trading days. Cost 0.05% per side. Baseline: random entries with the same exit on
every day in the same context (uptrend, plus the momentum filter where the rule has one). n < 30 = too few.

## Tests counted this round (3). Cumulative 123 + 3 = 126, Bonferroni alpha = 0.05/126 = 0.000397
R4-1 base pullback (close > SMA200 & RSI(2) < 10) on U4
R4-2 live Grade A rule: pullback & top 10 by 12-1 momentum at the last month-end, ranked among U4
R4-3 pullback & top decile (ceil(10% of ranked names) at that month-end), ranked among U4

Survival (each test): OOS n >= 30, binomial p (hit vs same-exit random) < 0.000397, OOS net expectancy > 0,
and TRAIN hit rate > TRAIN baseline (same direction in both periods).

## Descriptive checks (not counted as tests, reported for whichever rule survives)
* "new names only": U4 minus the 23 (does it work outside the names it was found on?)
* core 7 subset; per-year OOS; next-open entry; 3xATR stop; worst trade, PF, avg win/loss.

## Adoption rule for the live site (decided now)
Switch the live scanner/ranking to U4 only if ALL hold:
1. R4-2 (the exact live rule, top 10) survives. R4-3 is informational and will NOT replace top 10 even if better.
2. "new names only" R4-2 OOS hit > its baseline and net > 0 (descriptive, no p cut-off).
3. Next-open entry OOS net > 0 for R4-2.
4. Reliability: three batch downloads of all U4 daily bars each finish in <= 90 s with <= 2 tickers missing, and the
   full local build (all tickers, scanner + cards) stays under 4 minutes.
Otherwise keep the 23-ticker universe and say so.

## Known bias (disclosed whatever the result)
Survivorship / selection: U4 is TODAY's S&P 100, so the backtest only contains companies that ended up large. This
inflates absolute returns of any long rule, especially momentum. The random-entry baseline is drawn from the same
survivor universe, so the hit-rate comparison is relative, but the absolute net per trade is likely overstated.
